Windows: Fixed every file write being refused or asked about for projects on exFAT or FAT32 drives, including in sessions started with --plugin-dir
Improved startup time with many plugins enabled: plugin command and agent files now take far fewer file system calls to load, most of all on Windows
Improved auto mode with the server-side classifier: a conversation too long for the safety check is now compacted, instead of every checked tool call being denied
Improved the message when a background session reopened from another folder has no LLM gateway: it now says why, instead of "Not logged in"

Added the % motion to vim mode: jump to the matching bracket, alone or with d/c/y

Fixed quitting removing a worktree made by a WorktreeCreate hook without asking when it may hold unpushed commits
Fixed the fable (and best) model alias erroring on the Anthropic API when the newest Fable model is not available to your organization: Claude Code now retries once on the previous Fable model
Fixed a misleading "Please run /login" error when a full disk keeps the login from being refreshed; the error now names the disk and says to delete files

Fixed workflow agents sometimes skipping their step, and the run still reporting success, after reading the harness note that their task text carries no user authority
Fixed artifact updates being refused where a PreToolUse hook covers Edit or Write; Claude now edits the file and then republishes instead of changing it in the publish call
Fixed skills and commands with very many or very long argument names stalling for seconds when invoked; only the first 64 names, each up to 64 characters, are now filled in

- Open /config to search preferences across categories, change supported settings immediately, and see which changes require a restart. (#52990, #53429) - Send a follow-up while Codex is responding to steer it immediately.

The default is Ctrl+X, shortcut hints stay open until you choose or cancel, and voice mute moves to F9. (#52273) - Restart a managed background server from /daemon.

Codex warns about work the restart could interrupt, then reconnects automatically. (#53173) - Codex can run independent read-only tools in parallel, including skill, memory, and conversation-history lookups. (#52245) - Daybreak is enabled by default for eligible accounts. codex exec can also select it with an OpenAI API key when the server offers access. (#53701, #53717) - Resuming a saved thread restores its permissions and network approvals, while respecting explicit overrides and current managed policy. (#53150, #53419, #53424) - The network proxy now checks permission before a DNS lookup, rejects duplicate Host headers, and prevents credential aliases from bypassing inspection hooks. (#51650, #52661, #53506) - Return to an existing side conversation with /side after switching threads.
Answers to pending prompts also go back to the thread that asked. (#52184, #53436) - On Windows, Ctrl+V and Shift+Insert paste text as well as images.
On WSL, repeated pastes reuse the clipboard reader, and copy attempts time out instead of hanging. (#53224, #52967, #53453) - Local commands finish promptly when a child keeps an output pipe open.

Remote commands preserve late-arriving output so the final poll can still collect it. (#52652, #53331, #53622) - codex exec no longer prints the same file diff again after an unrelated command. (#53444) - Updated the bundled OpenAI Docs guidance for migrations to the GPT-6 family, including model-specific reasoning, tool use, and data residency considerations. (#51768) - Clarified how the Linux sandbox uses bubblewrap for filesystem isolation and seccomp for syscall filtering. (#52610) - Codex now uses its standard shell executor and no longer bundles a patched zsh.

Configurations using the retired shell flags receive a migration notice.
